For a 50:50 mixture **among accepted negatives**, define eligible items E = real catalog items minus the user’s training positives and current target; exclude padding. Compute wᵢ = training_countᵢ^0.75. For each negative, select uniform or weighted with probability 0.5 **once**, then retain that component throughout rejection. Derived distribution: P(i|E)=0.5/|E|+0.5wᵢ/Σⱼ∈Ewⱼ. Redrawing the component after every rejection instead conditions the global mixture on eligibility, changing accepted component proportions. These are distinct experimental definitions.

After bounded rejection attempts, sample directly from E using the selected component: uniform, or weights renormalized over E. This preserves the conditional distribution; an unconditional uniform fallback generally changes it. If E is empty, skip/mask the loss position or raise explicitly—never return a positive or padding as a valid negative. If eligible weighted mass is zero, that component is undefined; document a uniform fallback or restrict the catalog beforehand. For sampling without replacement, remove each accepted item from E across both components and recompute conditional probabilities; reject or explicitly cap requests exceeding |E|. A single fixed-mixture `choice(..., replace=False)` generally defines a different sequential distribution. [NumPy choice documentation](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/generated/numpy.random.Generator.choice.html).

Keep preprocessing seed 0 and training root seed 42. Spawn separate NumPy Generator streams for categories, workers, and sampling purposes using SeedSequence; avoid inherited generator copies. Give DataLoader a dedicated seeded torch.Generator; initialize worker-local NumPy generators through worker_init_fn using the worker’s PyTorch seed. Persistent workers retain RNG state across epochs. Fixed worker configuration/order supports repeatability; worker-count-independent sampling requires deterministic per-example/epoch/draw seeds. Keep diagnostics/evaluation streams separate. [NumPy parallel RNG](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/random/parallel.html), [PyTorch worker seeding](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/data.md).
